item.title: Elder Bhaddiya Kāḷigodhāyaputta (continued): Of few desires, persistent, Delighting in food placed in a bowl, Meditating, unattached, I am a son of Godha. Content, persistent,…
item.description:
Elder Bhaddiya Kāḷigodhāyaputta (continued):

Of few desires, persistent,
Delighting in food placed in a bowl,
Meditating, unattached,
I am a son of Godha.

Content, persistent,
Delighting in food placed in a bowl,
Meditating, unattached,
I am a son of Godha.

Practicing seclusion, persistent,
Delighting in food placed in a bowl,
Meditating, unattached,
I am a son of Godha.

Not associating, persistent,
Delighting in food placed in a bowl,
Meditating, unattached,
I am a son of Godha.

Dwelling energetically, persistent,
Delighting in food placed in a bowl,
Meditating, unattached,
I am a son of Godha.

Abandoning precious bowls of gold and fine resin,
I take a clay bowl —
This is my second consecration.

With high ramparts protecting,
With watchtowers and strong gates,
With soldiers holding swords,
I lived in fear.

Now virtuous, fearless,
Abandoning trembling and terror,
Meditating in the deep forest,
I am a son of Godha.

Established on the aggregate of virtue,
Mindful, developing insight wisdom,
Step by step I have attained
The destruction of all fetters.

From: Theragāthā 16.7

item.title: - Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings born of contact, with contact as their root, contact as their source, contact as their condition. What three?…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings born of contact, with contact as their root, contact as their source, contact as their condition. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. Just as, bhikkhus, when two sticks are rubbed together, brought into close contact, heat is generated and fire appears. When those two sticks are separated and the condition is cut off, the heat that arose from that condition ceases and is stilled. So too, bhikkhus, these three feelings are born of contact, with contact as their root, contact as their source, contact as their condition. In dependence on the corresponding contact, the corresponding feeling arises. With the cessation of the corresponding contact, the corresponding feeling ceases.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.10

item.title: Standing to one side, the devata Candana said this verse to the Blessed One: How to cross the flood, Steadfast day and night, Without standing,…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the devata Candana said this verse to the Blessed One:
How to cross the flood,
Steadfast day and night,
Without standing, without clinging,
Who does not sink in the deep?
( Blessed One ):
One always virtuous,
Wise, well concentrated,
With energy and strength,
Crosses the hard-to-cross flood.
One who abandons, leaves sensual perceptions,
Crosses beyond the bonds of form,
Destroys delight and craving for existence,
Does not sink in the deep.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.15

item.title: One who has no craving, Wise, without doubt, Who has realized the Deathless — Him I call a brahmin. One who here has transcended both…
item.description:
One who has no craving,
Wise, without doubt,
Who has realized the Deathless —
Him I call a brahmin.

One who here has transcended both good and evil,
Sorrowless, stainless, pure —
Him I call a brahmin.

Pure as the moon, unstained,
Clear, tranquil,
Who has destroyed delight in existence —
Him I call a brahmin.

Who has crossed this dangerous path,
Overcome delusion and saṃsāra,
Reached the far shore, meditative,
Without desire, without doubt,
Without grasping, at peace —
Him I call a brahmin.

From: Dhammapada 383-423

item.title: The Blessed One: I am not hired by anyone in the world, With what I have realized I wander the world, No wages are needed…
item.description:
The Blessed One:
I am not hired by anyone in the world,
With what I have realized I wander the world,
No wages are needed for me.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.2

item.title: Bhikkhus, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the four great kings themselves travel through this world to see: 'Among humans, are there many who…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, the four great kings themselves travel through this world to see: 'Among humans, are there many who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds?' If there are many among humans who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds, then the four great kings report to the devas of the Thirty-three who are sitting assembled in the Sudhammā assembly hall: 'Sirs, there are many among humans who respect their mother, respect their father, honor samaṇas and brahmins, honor the elders of the family, observe the Uposatha, are heedful, and do meritorious deeds.' Then, bhikkhus, the devas of the Thirty-three rejoice and say: 'Indeed, the deva host will increase, and the asura host will diminish!'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.37

item.title: At that time, the Blessed One's foot was cut by a stone splinter. Severe feelings arose in the Blessed One — painful, sharp, racking, fierce,…
item.description:
At that time, the Blessed One's foot was cut by a stone splinter. Severe feelings arose in the Blessed One — painful, sharp, racking, fierce, disagreeable, unpleasant. But the Blessed One endured them mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed. Then the Blessed One had his outer robe folded in four and laid down on his right side in the lion's posture, one foot on the other, mindful and clearly comprehending.

Standing to one side, a devata spoke this inspired utterance before the Blessed One:
- Samaṇa Gotama is truly a bull elephant. And as a bull elephant, he endures bodily feelings that arise — painful, sharp, racking, fierce, disagreeable, unpleasant — mindfully and clearly comprehending, without being distressed.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.38

item.title: This wise bhikkhu should gather the fundamental Dhamma, Guard the senses, know moderation, Guard the fundamental virtues, Frequent good friends, Live purely and diligently. Being…
item.description:
This wise bhikkhu should gather the fundamental Dhamma,
Guard the senses, know moderation,
Guard the fundamental virtues,
Frequent good friends,
Live purely and diligently.

Being courteous and friendly,
Conducting oneself properly,
Thus one gains great joy,
And will make an end of suffering.

Like the jasmine flower sheds its withered petals,
So, bhikkhu, abandon greed and hatred.

From: Dhammapada 360-382

item.description:
Elder Vanavaccha:

Covered by Indra's herdsmen, those rocky mountains delight my mind.

item.title: Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must know moderation in eating. Reflecting wisely, we take food not for enjoyment, not for…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, what are the further tasks to be done? 'We must know moderation in eating. Reflecting wisely, we take food not for enjoyment, not for indulgence, not for beautification, not for ornamentation, but only for the support and maintenance of this body, for avoiding harm, for assisting the holy life, thinking: "Thus I shall destroy old feelings and not arouse new feelings; and there will be for me blamelessness and a comfortable abiding."' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāassapurasutta
